presentingComplaint: 3 days of fever, productive cough with rust-coloured sputum and right-sided pleuritic chest pain
history: 59-year-old man with rheumatoid arthritis on long-term methotrexate 15 mg weekly plus prednisolone 10 mg daily, presenting with 3 days of fever, rigors, productive cough with rust-coloured sputum and right-sided pleuritic chest pain. Mild breathlessness on exertion but no orthopnoea, haemoptysis or weight loss. No recent hospitalisation, no antibiotics in the last 90 days and no ICU stay. No aspiration event, choking or dysphagia; swallow is normal. No prior TB, no known TB contact and no evening fever or night sweats. Ex-smoker (20 pack-years), lives at home independently, not from an endemic malaria area and no recent travel. Because he is immunosuppressed (steroid + methotrexate), he was started on broad empiric cover pending cultures, with a plan to narrow once a pathogen was identified.
examination: Alert and oriented, mildly unwell but not toxic. Respiratory exam reveals reduced expansion and bronchial breathing with coarse crepitations over the right lower zone and dullness to percussion; no bronchial breathing elsewhere. No oral thrush or mucositis. Cardiovascular exam normal with no murmur. Abdomen soft, no organomegaly. No rash, no calf tenderness, no lymphadenopathy.
imaging: Chest radiograph: dense right lower lobe consolidation with air bronchograms and a small associated parapneumonic effusion; no cavitation, no multilobar involvement, no upper-lobe fibrocavitary disease.
microbiology: Pneumococcal urinary antigen positive. Blood cultures x2 sent on admission; sputum Gram stain shows Gram-positive diplococci with abundant neutrophils. Sputum culture at 48h grew penicillin-susceptible Streptococcus pneumoniae (penicillin MIC 0.03 mg/L; ceftriaxone and amoxicillin susceptible). Two sputum AFB smears negative; respiratory viral PCR (including influenza and SARS-CoV-2) negative.
differentialDiagnoses: Community-acquired pneumonia (pneumococcal) — favoured: lobar consolidation, rust-coloured sputum, positive pneumococcal urinary antigen and culture
Aspiration pneumonia — no aspiration event, dysphagia or dependent-segment/foul-smelling disease
Pulmonary tuberculosis — no chronic cough, night sweats, upper-lobe cavitation; smears negative
Lung abscess — no cavitating lesion or foul sputum on imaging
finalDiagnosis: Non-severe community-acquired pneumonia due to penicillin-susceptible Streptococcus pneumoniae in an immunocompromised host (methotrexate + corticosteroid), managed as an inpatient with initial broad empiric cover then de-escalation
citations: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Pneumonia
stewardship: Immunosuppression (methotrexate plus daily prednisolone) prompts broader initial empiric cover and inpatient management despite a low severity score (CURB-65 1, non-ICU). Empiric therapy per ATS/IDSA 2019 for a non-severe inpatient without pseudomonal/MRSA risk factors: a beta-lactam (ceftriaxone) plus a macrolide (azithromycin) for atypical cover, or respiratory fluoroquinolone monotherapy. Once pneumococcal urinary antigen and sputum culture confirmed penicillin-susceptible S. pneumoniae with no atypical/resistant pathogen, therapy was de-escalated to targeted amoxicillin (or IV benzylpenicillin) and the macrolide stopped. Total 5-day course given clinical stability and defervescence; switch IV-to-oral once afebrile and haemodynamically stable with functioning GI tract.
contraindications: Macrolide caution with QT-prolonging drugs and known long-QT
Fluoroquinolones associated with tendinopathy, QT prolongation and dysglycaemia — avoid as first choice if beta-lactam/macrolide feasible
Continue folic acid; withhold/adjust methotrexate during acute infection per rheumatology advice
edgeCases: Immunocompromise widens the differential to opportunistic pathogens (Pneumocystis, Nocardia, fungi) if lobar consolidation does not respond or diffuse/atypical infiltrates appear
Positive pneumococcal urinary antigen may persist after recent infection — correlate with culture before over-interpreting
If parapneumonic effusion enlarges or patient fails to improve, sample the pleural fluid to exclude empyema
expectedMaiK: Non-severe CAP in an immunocompromised host: confirm lobar consolidation, start guideline-concordant empiric therapy with broader initial cover given immunosuppression, then de-escalate to pathogen-directed penicillin once S. pneumoniae is confirmed.
